explanation: Encoding groups each maximal run and writes its decimal length followed by its character. Decoding accumulates all digits of the next length, then repeats the following nondigit character and resets the count.
timeComplexity: O(n + m) for input length n and produced output length m. Encoding visits each input character once; decoding scans count digits and emits every decoded character once.
spaceComplexity: O(m) output storage. The builders store the produced output, whose decoded length may greatly exceed encoded length.
attribution: Unmodified reference from epi_judge_python_solutions/run_length_compression.py; Elements of Programming Interviews Judge contributors; CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 International, retained in repository LICENSE. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: Encoding partitions the input into maximal equal-character runs, so each written count/character pair describes exactly one run. During decoding, count contains all decimal digits since the previous character; emitting that many copies reconstructs the corresponding run and resets the invariant. Nondigit input characters make the representation unambiguous.
walkthrough: For decoded text "qqqqqqqqqqqqrr", Encoding counts twelve q characters and two r characters, returning "12q2r". Decoding accumulates digits 1 then 2 into count 12, emits twelve q characters, then emits two r characters. Both directions recover the other value.
edgeCases: Empty text encodes and decodes to empty text.
Run lengths may contain several decimal digits.
A singleton run still writes count 1.
Original text characters must be nondigits.
